ratings.Rationale: Readiness reports built from manual monthly data pulls are not predictive, and deferring RMF controls until after award puts the authorization to operate at risk. Significant weakness on the most important factor.
The Program Manager is a contingent hire, and quality control rests on a quarterly satisfaction survey with no measurable service levels. Transition meets 60 days, but staffing risk is high.
A standard data model mapping GCSS-Army and legacy STAMIS feeds is sound, but the approach assumes continuous network access and offers nothing for units operating disconnected. Meets requirements.
A 45-day phased transition beats the 60-day requirement and the Program Manager is on staff. The Lead Data Scientist is not yet named, a minor risk the rest of the plan offsets.

Predictive maintenance models validated on three years of Army fleet data cut unscheduled maintenance 18 percent in a pilot, GCSS-Army integration is already RMF-authorized, and disconnected units keep a local node. Exceptional, very low risk.
Both key personnel are current employees committed full time from award, transition completes in 55 days, and a monthly quality review with the COR tracks corrective actions. Exceeds requirements.
Monthly manual extracts from GCSS-Army cannot support failure forecasting, and RMF work does not start until after award. The approach is unlikely to meet the requirement without major rework.
With the Program Manager still a contingent hire and quality measured only by a quarterly survey, the management approach carries significant risk despite a compliant 60-day transition.

The unified data model across GCSS-Army and STAMIS feeds, refreshed every four hours, is a meaningful strength. The missing disconnected-operations approach is a weakness, but one I see as correctable.
The phased 45-day transition by installation and an on-staff Program Manager reduce startup risk. Quality control follows an established ISO 9001 process.

Field-validated predictive maintenance with transparent model accuracy, an already-authorized GCSS-Army interface, and local nodes for disconnected units. The strongest and lowest-risk technical approach.
Named, committed key personnel from day one, a 55-day transition that moves open work orders first, and a measurable monthly quality review make this an exceptional management approach.
Manual monthly extracts and after-award RMF work leave both predictive analytics and authorization unaddressed. A significant weakness on the most important factor.
The only reference is a small commercial trucking-fleet reporting job with no CPARS. Recent but of limited relevance to Army logistics, so confidence is low.
The integrated data model is solid, but assuming continuous connectivity leaves deployed and disconnected units without analytics. Acceptable overall.
A Very Good CPARS on a relevant DLA supply-chain analytics effort supports a reasonable expectation of success; the second reference is only Satisfactory and Navy-focused.

Strong, field-validated predictive models and an authorized GCSS-Army interface. I rate it Good because the RMF plan relies on controls inherited from the Army cloud without saying which remain the offeror's.
Exceptional CPARS on a current Army Materiel Command readiness analytics effort, plus a Very Good predictive-maintenance pilot. Recent, highly relevant and high quality.

All three evaluators unanimously rated this Marginal, citing retrospective-only monthly reporting via manual GCSS-Army extracts, silence on legacy STAMIS feed integration, and a significant weakness for deferring all RMF control implementation until after award. These findings reflect a proposal that fails to meet several solicitation requirements with high risk of unsuccessful performance absent government intervention.

Both evaluators rating this factor (Marcus Reyes, Priya Natarajan) agree on Marginal, driven by a significant weakness for an unfilled, contingent-hire Program Manager position and additional weaknesses for an unnamed/unqualified staff, a vague transition-in plan, and quality control limited to a quarterly survey with no measurable standards.

Only Tom Okafor recorded a rating for this factor, citing a single, low-relevance commercial trucking-fleet reference with no CPARS record, no narrative discussion of past performance, and no description of scope, technical complexity, or performance history, supporting a Limited Confidence rating.

Marcus Reyes and Tom Okafor rated Acceptable while Priya Natarajan rated Good; all three cite the same findings, including a significant weakness for assuming continuous network access for every unit, which directly undermines operations in disconnected/degraded environments central to this factor. Because the significant weakness and associated connectivity risk are substantive and shared across all evaluators, the rating best supported by the findings is Acceptable, consistent with the majority and the severity of the significant weakness.

Marcus Reyes and Priya Natarajan unanimously rated Good, supported by a strength for completing transition-in in 45 days (ahead of the 60-day requirement) and an on-staff Program Manager, offset by weaknesses regarding the unidentified Lead Data Scientist and a general quality control description.

Only Tom Okafor recorded a rating, citing a Very Good CPARS on a relevant $9.6M DLA supply-chain analytics effort as a strength, offset by a second, lower-rated (Satisfactory) and less relevant reference, and a thin two-page submission lacking narrative discussion and a third reference.

Marcus Reyes and Priya Natarajan rated Outstanding while Tom Okafor rated Good; all three cite identical strengths (field-validated predictive maintenance models with transparent accuracy/drift reporting, a disconnected-operations plan) and identical weaknesses/risk (an unsubstantiated 'already authorized' GCSS-Army claim, no RMF milestone plan, and reliance on unspecified inherited cloud controls). Because the strengths are multiple, significant, and exceed requirements while the weaknesses are process/documentation gaps rather than approach failures, the findings best support Outstanding, consistent with the majority.

Marcus Reyes rated Good and Priya Natarajan rated Outstanding, both citing the same findings: two current, full-time-committed named key personnel, a 55-day transition prioritizing open work orders, and a measurable monthly quality metric, offset by weaknesses including no backup/succession plan and a thinly described quality control process. Given the weaknesses noted by both evaluators (sparse QC description, no succession planning) are substantive and shared, the rating best supported by the findings is Good rather than Outstanding.

Priya Natarajan's Poor rating relies on the identical Significant Weakness finding but weighs the added staff workload more heavily; because the deficiency is a Significant Weakness rather than a Deficiency and LTI 1.3 support remains a Strength (-A6), Satisfactory is the better-supported rating.

Both evaluators (Marcus Reyes, Priya Natarajan) unanimously rated this Satisfactory, 12 of 20 points, citing a workable but under-specified implementation plan, limited on-demand-only teacher training (Weakness -A3), and a Significant Weakness in support desk hours (8 a.m.-5 p.m. Eastern) that falls short of the District's needs (-A4). SOURCE SELECTION DECISION DOCUMENT
Solicitation No. W52P1J-27-R-0023
Army Logistics Data Analytics Platform
Department of the Army

1. ACQUISITION AND BASIS FOR AWARD

This acquisition is for an Army Logistics Data Analytics Platform under Solicitation W52P1J-27-R-0023. Award will be made on a best-value tradeoff basis pursuant to FAR 15.101-1. The evaluation factors and their relative order of importance are: Technical Approach (F1), Management Approach (F2), and Past Performance (F3), all of which combined are significantly more important than Price. Technical Approach is more important than Management Approach; Management Approach and Past Performance are of equal importance to each other.

Three offerors submitted proposals: Bluestem Data Systems Corp, Ironwood Federal Solutions Inc, and Keystone Ridge Analytics LLC.

2. EVALUATION SUMMARY

The SSEB Consensus Report, dated and filed with the official award record for Solicitation W52P1J-27-R-0023, is incorporated herein by reference in its entirety. All factor-level strengths, weaknesses, significant weaknesses, risks, and rating rationales are set forth in that report and are not repeated here. The consensus ratings and total evaluated prices are summarized below:

  Offeror                          F1-Tech    F2-Mgmt    F3-Past Perf    Total Evaluated Price
  Bluestem Data Systems Corp       Marginal   Marginal   Ltd Confidence  $15,500,000
  Ironwood Federal Solutions Inc   Acceptable Good       Sat Confidence  $16,550,000
  Keystone Ridge Analytics LLC     Outstanding Good      Sub Confidence  $19,300,000

IGCE variance: Bluestem -14.84% (CLIN 0005 flagged as unbalanced: $1,700,000 vs. IGCE $1,000,000); Ironwood -9.07% (no unbalanced CLINs); Keystone +6.04% (no unbalanced CLINs).

3. COMPARATIVE ASSESSMENT

The following findings from the SSEB Consensus Report discriminate meaningfully among offerors on the most important factors. All citations are to the offeror's proposal volume and page as recorded in the consensus record.

Technical Approach (F1) — Most Important Factor

3.1 Keystone vs. Ironwood (Technical): Keystone's proposal presents field-validated predictive maintenance models trained on three years of Army equipment data and a local analytics node architecture that explicitly addresses disconnected operations (technical p.2–3, findings W52P1J-27-R-0023-KEYSTONE-F1-A1-E1, -A3-E1). Ironwood's proposal, by contrast, contains a significant weakness for assuming continuous network connectivity for every unit, a condition that does not reflect Army operational realities, and does not describe how legacy STAMIS feeds will be reconciled with GCSS-Army data (technical p.3, findings W52P1J-27-R-0023-IRONWOOD-F1-A2-E1, -A3-E1). This gap represents a meaningful technical advantage for Keystone on the most important factor.

3.2 Keystone vs. Bluestem (Technical): Bluestem's proposal is rated Marginal, driven by retrospective-only monthly reporting via manual GCSS-Army extracts, silence on legacy STAMIS integration, and a significant weakness for deferring all RMF control implementation until after award (technical p.2–4, findings W52P1J-27-R-0023-BLUESTEM-F1-A2-E1, -A3-E1, -A4-E1). Keystone's Outstanding rating reflects a substantially superior technical solution across predictive analytics capability, data integration, and disconnected-operations support.

3.3 Ironwood vs. Bluestem (Technical): Ironwood's Acceptable rating, while carrying its own significant weakness regarding connectivity assumptions, is materially stronger than Bluestem's Marginal rating, which reflects multiple weaknesses and a significant weakness on cybersecurity posture (technical p.4, finding W52P1J-27-R-0023-BLUESTEM-F1-A4-E1).

Management Approach (F2) — Equal Second in Importance

3.4 Ironwood and Keystone vs. Bluestem (Management): Both Ironwood and Keystone received Good ratings under Management Approach. Bluestem received Marginal, driven by a significant weakness for an unfilled Program Manager position supported only by a contingent-hire arrangement (management p.2, finding W52P1J-27-R-0023-BLUESTEM-F2-A1-E1). This represents a meaningful discriminator separating Bluestem from both higher-rated offerors.

3.5 Ironwood vs. Keystone (Management): Both offerors are rated Good. Ironwood's proposal commits to a 45-day transition-in, 15 days ahead of the stated requirement (management p.2, finding W52P1J-27-R-0023-IRONWOOD-F2-A2-E1). Keystone names two current, full-time-committed key personnel but does not address succession or backup plans (management p.2, findings W52P1J-27-R-0023-KEYSTONE-F2-A1-E1, -A4-E1). The Management Approach ratings are essentially equivalent; no meaningful discriminator separates Ironwood from Keystone on this factor.

Past Performance (F3) — Equal Second in Importance

3.6 Keystone vs. Ironwood (Past Performance): Keystone holds Substantial Confidence, anchored by an Exceptional CPARS on the current $14.2M AMC Readiness Analytics effort — a directly relevant Army logistics analytics program (pastPerformance p.2, finding W52P1J-27-R-0023-KEYSTONE-F3-A1-E3). Ironwood holds Satisfactory Confidence, with a Very Good CPARS on a $9.6M DLA supply-chain analytics effort offset by a Satisfactory CPARS on a second reference (pastPerformance p.2, findings W52P1J-27-R-0023-IRONWOOD-F3-A1-E3, -A4-E3). Keystone's past performance record is meaningfully stronger.

3.7 Ironwood vs. Bluestem (Past Performance): Ironwood's Satisfactory Confidence is substantially stronger than Bluestem's Limited Confidence, which rests on a single commercial trucking-fleet reference with no CPARS record and no demonstrated relevance to Army logistics data analytics (pastPerformance p.2, findings W52P1J-27-R-0023-BLUESTEM-F3-A1-E3, -A2-E3).

Price

3.8 Keystone's total evaluated price of $19,300,000 represents a $2,750,000 premium over Ironwood ($16,550,000) and a $3,800,000 premium over Bluestem ($15,500,000). Keystone's price is 6.04% above the IGCE and carries no unbalanced CLINs. Bluestem's price is 14.84% below the IGCE and has CLIN 0005 (Transition-in) flagged as unbalanced at $1,700,000 against an IGCE of $1,000,000, introducing performance risk. Ironwood's price is 9.07% below the IGCE with no unbalanced CLINs.

4. TRADEOFF ANALYSIS

Technical Approach is the most important factor, and it is the primary discriminator in this competition. Keystone Ridge Analytics LLC is the only offeror rated Outstanding on Technical Approach, reflecting field-validated predictive models, a model-registry transparency mechanism, and an explicit disconnected-operations architecture — capabilities that directly address the Army's core requirements. Ironwood's Acceptable rating reflects a significant weakness on connectivity assumptions that creates meaningful schedule and operational risk. Bluestem's Marginal rating on Technical Approach, compounded by a Marginal on Management Approach and Limited Confidence on Past Performance, places it outside the competitive range for best-value consideration.

On the second-tier factors (Management Approach and Past Performance, equal in importance), Keystone and Ironwood are both rated Good on Management Approach with no meaningful discriminator between them. On Past Performance, Keystone's Substantial Confidence — grounded in an Exceptional CPARS on a current, large, directly relevant Army program — is a meaningful advantage over Ironwood's Satisfactory Confidence.

Keystone's $2,750,000 price premium over Ironwood (approximately 16.6%) must be weighed against its advantages. Given that all non-price factors combined are significantly more important than price, and given that Keystone holds a clear advantage on the most important factor (Outstanding vs. Acceptable on Technical Approach) and a meaningful advantage on Past Performance (Substantial vs. Satisfactory Confidence), the non-price benefits associated with Keystone's proposal are assessed as worth the price premium. Keystone's price is reasonable relative to the IGCE (+6.04%) and carries no unbalanced CLINs.

Bluestem's lower price ($15,500,000) does not offset its Marginal ratings on the two highest-weighted non-price factors and its unbalanced CLIN 0005. Bluestem does not represent best value.

This analysis supports award to Keystone Ridge Analytics LLC as providing the best value to the Government.

5. DECISION

Based on my review of the SSEB Consensus Report, the price analysis and the tradeoff analysis above, I select Keystone Ridge Analytics LLC for award as the best value to the Government.

Keystone Ridge Analytics LLC is rated Outstanding in Technical Approach, Good in Management Approach and Substantial Confidence in Past Performance, at a total evaluated price of $19,300,000 (6.0% above the IGCE).

Bluestem Data Systems Corp is $3,800,000 (24.5%) lower in price but rated lower in Technical Approach (40%), Management Approach (25%) and Past Performance (25%); I find Keystone Ridge Analytics LLC's advantages worth the premium.

Ironwood Federal Solutions Inc is $2,750,000 (16.6%) lower in price but rated lower in Technical Approach (40%) and Past Performance (25%); I find Keystone Ridge Analytics LLC's advantages worth the premium.

This decision reflects my independent judgment.

/s/ James Thornton
James Thornton
Source Selection Authority
Department of the Army
